title: First steps
intro:
Your robot runs real Python. `move()` moves it one square forward.

Get it to the flag.

title: Round the corner
intro:
`turn_left()` and `turn_right()` turn the robot on the spot (they don't move it).

The little arrow shows which way it's facing.

title: Shiny things
intro:
`collect()` picks up the gem the robot is standing on. Grab them all for a star!

Careful: grabbing where there's no gem makes the robot drop everything.

title: The long hallway
intro:
Ten `move()` lines would work... but a `for` loop does it in two:

```python
for i in range(3):
    move()
```

That moves 3 times. How many do you need?

title: Gem run
intro:
A loop can repeat more than one line. Everything indented under the `for` is repeated.

The flag is one step past the last gem.

title: Staircase
intro:
Spot the pattern: the stairs repeat the same few moves over and over.

Put one step of the staircase inside a loop.

title: Gem or no gem?
intro:
Your code runs on **two worlds** with gems in different places, so you can't just memorize them.

`on_gem()` is `True` when the robot stands on a gem:

```python
if on_gem():
    collect()
```

title: How far is it?
intro:
Two worlds again, and the hallways are different lengths. A `for` loop needs to know how many times, a `while` loop doesn't:

```python
while not at_goal():
    ...
```

It keeps going until `at_goal()` is `True`.

title: Follow the wall
intro:
`front_is_clear()` is `True` when there's no wall right in front of the robot.

In both worlds the path turns **left** at every wall. Go forward when you can, turn when you can't:

```python
if front_is_clear():
    ...
else:
    ...
```

title: Treasure path
intro: Same idea as the last level, but now there are gems scattered along the way. Grab every one, in both worlds.

title: Broken gears
intro:
Oh no, this robot's `turn_right()` is broken! It can only turn left.

Three lefts make a right. Teach the robot a new command with `def`:

```python
def turn_right():
    ...
```

Then use it like any other command.

title: The Labyrinth
intro:
The final level: two different mazes, one program.

A famous trick solves any maze like these: keep your **right hand on the wall**. Each step, turn right, then turn left until the way ahead is clear, then move.
